papers.title: Heat treatment effect on the microstructure and corrosion behavior of 316L stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting for proton exchange membrane fuel cells
papers.first_author_affiliation: Corrosion and Protection Center, Key Laboratory for Corrosion and Protection (MOE), University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing 100083, China

corresponding_authors.name: Chaofang Dong
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Corrosion and Protection Center, Key Laboratory for Corrosion and Protection (MOE), University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing 100083, China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究用于燃料电池的316L不锈钢的腐蚀行为，与生物医学植入物方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implants, porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue, osseointegration, or any mechanical testing relevant to AM biomedical materials.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究热处理对SLM 316L不锈钢在燃料电池环境中腐蚀行为的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用不同热处理工艺处理SLM 316L样品，进行电化学腐蚀测试。
summary_zh.result: 热处理显著影响显微组织和耐腐蚀性，优化的热处理改善了腐蚀性能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过电化学测试和微观结构表征验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of heat treatment on the corrosion behavior of selective laser melted 316L stainless steel in a proton exchange membrane fuel cell environment.
summary_en.method: Different heat treatment protocols were applied to SLM 316L samples, followed by electrochemical corrosion testing and microstructural analysis.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment significantly altered the microstructure and corrosion resistance, with optimized treatments enhancing performance.
summary_en.validation: Validation via electrochemical measurements and microstructure characterization.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how selective laser melting parameters affect Mg2Si precipitation and Si spheroidization in AlSi10Mg alloy.
summary_en.method: Variation of laser power and scanning speed followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Process parameters strongly influence the formation of Mg2Si precipitates and the spheroidization of Si particles.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural analysis using SEM, XRD, and mechanical property tests confirm the observed trends.

papers.title: 3D Bioprinting and Decellularized ECM-Based Biomaterials for in Vitro  CV Tissue Engineering
papers.abstract: Advanced extrusion-based 3D printing strategies allow the rapid fabrication of complex anatomically relevant architectures. Moreover, they have the potential to fabricate 3D-bioprinted cardiac constructs by depositing cardiac cells with appropriate biomaterials. Heart-derived decellularized extracellular matrices containing a complex mixture of various extracellular molecules provide a comprehensive microenvironmental niche similar to native cardiac tissue. Nonetheless, a major concern persists pertaining to insufficient vascularization and mimicking of the complex 3D architectural features, which can be tackled using 3D printing approaches. In this review, we discuss the advantage and application of decellularized extracellular matrix-based hydrogels for the 3D printing of engineered cardiac tissues. We also briefly talk about the integration of electroactive materials within cardiac patches to improve the myocardium's electrophysiological properties.
